environment: Linux; Git 2.34.1; local bare repositories as remotes; Python 3.11 (vibe-coding env)
rounds: 9 rounds: rounds 1-8 NO-GO (each found a real A-class bypass), round 9 GO with A-class = 0
convergence_rule: an A-class finding is 'reports pushed while the real remote never received the ledger, or data loss'; A-class = 0 is GO, B-class items are advisory
a_class_findings_closed: round 1: a staged-but-unchanged ledger made the archive report no-changes while the local ledger was ahead
round 2: the index ledger could differ from the local ledger while unrelated files still staged
round 3: a clean filter or EOL conversion could rewrite the ledger on the way into Git
round 4: a bare push obeyed remote.<name>.push / push.default and could publish an unrelated ref
round 5: an unverifiable remote probe was treated as 'the remote does not have the commit'
round 6: git pushurl / self-referential target handling could self-satisfy the verification
round 7: a linked worktree of the knowledge base was not recognised as the same repository
round 8: file:// URLs with a non-canonical authority skipped the self-reference check
round 9: a ~ home-relative target was never expanded, so ~/kb resolved to the knowledge base while the push reported success
round_9_verification: the ~/kb repro now fails before commit and copy; external bare remote holds no ledger; KB worktree stays clean
additional ~ forms replayed (~//kb, ~///kb, ~/./kb, ~/foo/../kb with foo existing, ~, home/~/kb) without finding a new bypass
B3 fallback re-tested with a Git wrapper that rejects --path-format=absolute: --git-common-dir yields the same common dir for the main and linked worktree
29 archive tests, 263 total tests, package validation and git diff --check all pass on commit 4af95d5
reviewer reported git status --porcelain empty (read-only audit)
residual_advisory: B2: branch.<name>.remote configured with a URL instead of a remote name is reported as 'no such remote'; fail-closed but the message is misleading
very old Git without --git-common-dir is not covered; Windows/UNC behaviour is not covered
network schemes (SSH/HTTPS) are treated as external by design; a loopback remote is not proven unreachable by this design
supersedes: REVIEW-OPENCODE-008 recorded the same round-9 GO verdict but failed to bind EV-OPENCODE-011 because the evidence-reference flag was omitted; this revision binds it. The verdict and reviewer are unchanged.
